In a complete lattice, sSup ∅ = ⊥ is a theorem. In a conditionally complete lattice, this is not so, since not all conditionally complete lattices have a bottom element. What I find odd is that this isn't a theorem even in the cases that the conditionally complete lattice does have a bottom element. In fact, we have a separate typeclass docs#ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrderBot for precisely the conditionally complete linear orders which have a bottom satisfying sSup ∅ = ⊥.

My idea is to extend docs#ConditionallyCompleteLattice with two new fields IsBot x → sSup ∅ = x and IsTop x → sInf ∅ = x. i.e. we don't presume that the structure has a supremum/infimum, but if it does, we require that it has the correct value. Then we wouldn't need the bespoke ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrderBot, and we wouldn't have to always treat sSup ∅ as just a junk value.

Note that we don't need the analogous IsTop x → sSup univ = x, since that one is a theorem of conditionally complete lattices.

This came up in #38192. The intention of that PR is to split conditionally complete lattices into conditionally complete inf/sup semilattices, and I was wondering if we could adopt this same design there.

This is sort of related to an earlier idea of making a LawfulSup typeclass IsLUB x s → sSup s = x. If we did this, we'd have LawfulSup + OrderBot → sSup ∅ = ⊥. Then a ConditionallyCompleteLattice is LawfulSup + LawfulInf + all nonempty sets bounded above/below have a supremum/infimum. And all is good.
#38266 also seems relevant to this discussion
That PR implements a ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrderBot on Iio intervals, given such an instance on the original type
The issue is that some Iio intervals can be complete lattices proper, and in that case, the instance gives some wrong values
#37082 is intended to fix this issue. Alternatively, we could drop def-eq and define it using Classical.choice, like OrderSupInfSet.choose in #35674 or sSup in this branch.
